# @wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub
**Skills Hub** is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds a native, first-class panel to the web G
UI for discovering, installing, and managing Agent Skills.
It ships three capabilities in one panel:
- **Market** — search online skill registries (default: skillhub.cn, plus skills.sh and any public G
itHub repository), preview a skill's full documentation, and read its file manifest before deciding

to install.
- **My Skills** — browse every skill the runtime has loaded, grouped by source; enable o
r disable skills, edit their `SKILL.md`, or remove them (deletes go to `.trash`, never straight to d

isk loss).
- **Create** — write a new skill into the user-level or project-level skill root, with fr
ontmatter handling handled for you.
The panel reads the official skill roots (`<project>/.dsh/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, `~/.d
sh/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, plus any configured `customSkillDirs`) and merges the host's skill r
egistry on top, so what the panel displays is exactly what the model receives.

| Status | Market search & preview: **available**. Skill installation: planned (see Roadmap). |
| Re

quires | DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` |
| License | BSD-3-Clause |
| Languages | English, 简体中文 (follows the G
UI language setting) |

## Usage
### Market tab
Type a query and press Enter. The source picker to the left of the search field selects which regist
ry the search asks; the choice applies to the next search, so results always match the query that pr
h asks; the choice applies to the next search, so results always match the query that produced them.
- **skillhub.cn** (default) — a China-hosted skill store with 190,000+ skills, reachable directly wi
th no network accelerator. The site explicitly invites agent integration: it publishes an agent-faci
ng integration document (`install/skillhub.md`), allows crawlers in `robots.txt`, and its read path

is unauthenticated. Rows carry Chinese descriptions, download counts, and icons.
- **skills.sh** — t
he Agent Skills registry's search endpoint. This source serves one page; the panel says so honestly

instead of offering a load-more control that could only return empty.
- **GitHub repositories** — a
repository can also be browsed directly: any `owner/repo` (a full URL or a `.git` suffix also works)
is enumerated through the GitHub API, and every skill directory inside it becomes a row.
Long result lists load the next page automatically as you scroll, with an explicit "load more" butto
n as the keyboard/click target. Selecting a skill's name opens a detail dialog rendered by the shell
's own markdown renderer — the skill reads exactly as it does in a conversation — alongside its file
list and total size.

## Security model
- **Every route sits behind the shared loopback fence** (socket address + `Host` header + browser sa
me-origin markers). An unpaired LAN client receives `403 forbidden: loopback-only` before any skill
file is touched. When `dsh-remote-web-ui` is loaded, a live paired-device cookie is an additional al

low path; unpaired and revoked devices still receive 403.
- **A client-submitted `path` is only an i
dentity claim.** Before touching any file, the host re-scans and requires the same skill name to res
olve to that exact path. A project skill that disappeared can therefore never be redirected onto a s

ame-named user skill, and the routes cannot be used to read or write an arbitrary path.
- **The brow
ser never sends a URL.** Market requests carry only the opaque skill id the host issued; repositorie
s, refs, directories and file paths are re-derived host-side, and the id grammar is validated segmen

t by segment, so a path traversal is rejected before it can reach any fetch.
- **Remote fetching hap
pens only in the host half**, behind the trust fence. The unauthenticated GitHub API allows 60 reque
sts/hour, so only discovery (tree listing) touches it, cached for 30 minutes; file bodies come from
`raw.githubusercontent.com` through an accelerator chain, which does not count against that budget.

skillhub.cn is reached directly.
- **Registry icons are proxied, not linked.** Icon URLs are fetched
host-side under an explicit policy (https only, allow-listed host, image content-type, 256 KB cap)
and re-served as data URLs, so the browser never loads a third-party origin: no referrer leak, no tr

acking pixel per render.
- **Installs re-derive everything from the id.** The install route receives
only the opaque skill id and the workspace the panel is showing; the file list comes from the skill
's own detail manifest (never client-supplied), the target directory is derived host-side, and every
manifest path is validated before it is joined onto the staging root. An install can therefore only

write a skill directory under a skill root.
[该节后续省略]
## Architecture
The package is a dual-half DSH plugin:
- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`, runs in the DSH server process) — serves the `/api/skills-hub/*` ro

ute family, owns all network access, file I/O, and the trust fence.
- **Client half** (`lib/client.j
s`, runs in the web GUI) — registers the sidebar entry and the center-column page through the shell'
s official slot seats (`sidebar.panellist` and the keyed `main` slot), so the shell owns the row box
, active highlight and panel switching exactly as it does for its own Plugins and Schedule pages.
The client is built only on the host's frozen browser module table (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-*`); every control is the official shared primitive (`Button`, `Switch`,
`Input`, `Menu`, `Modal`, `MarkdownText`, …) — nothing is hand-drawn. Registration failures are log
ged and degrade the panel; they never fail the GUI's boot.
